BiblicalUsage: The slope is the hillside running down to the plain, and it is used for the borders of the land. Moses gives Reuben the plain under the springs of Pisgah, Joshua smites all the country of the hills and the south and the vale and the springs, and the kings he defeats are listed by the same country, hills and valleys and springs.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the springs and slopes are named so often because the land is the promise made visible: every hillside and spring has its place in the gift, and the God who promised the land knows it hill by hill. And I hold that the God who counts the slopes is the God who keeps the promise, down to the last spring in the valley.
